# ranwhat

> ranwhat is an open-source command-line tool for AI agent security on a developer's own machine. It reads the history Claude Code and nineteen other coding agents write to disk as an audit trail and reports what each agent actually did: credential reads, destructive commands, package publishing and other risky actions. It scans that history for leaked credentials (secret scanning for agent transcripts), scores what an agent's credentials allow, and flags the grants never used where the provider keeps a record. MIT licence, Python 3.9 or newer, no dependencies.

Run it without installing: `uvx ranwhat check`. Or install it: `pipx install ranwhat` or `pip install ranwhat`. No account is needed.

What goes online: `live` and `--pull-usage` ask only the provider that issued each token, and `update` only fetches the capability catalogue, sending the subscription token and nothing else. Everything else reads locally and sends nothing. There is no telemetry.

Where it fits: ranwhat is the after-the-fact side of AI agent security and developer OPSEC. It shows what already ran, what leaked to disk, and what the tokens still allow. It does not block actions while an agent works unless you install its opt-in Claude Code hook (`ranwhat hook install`), and it does not detect prompt injection or scan MCP servers and skills for malicious content.

Commands:

- `ranwhat check`: watch and clean in one read-only pass. It never changes anything.
- `ranwhat watch`: nine rules over what the agent ran: credential access, secret-shaped strings in tool calls, package publishing, cloud resource changes, financial API calls, log or history tampering, destructive git, recursive deletion, and local files uploaded with curl. `--json` prints one record per flagged call.
- `ranwhat clean`: finds credentials in every agent's transcripts, passwords typed into commands (`mysql -pPASSWORD`, `curl -u user:password`) among them, says what to rotate, and masks them only when asked (`--apply`, or `mask` in the review session). Backups go to `~/.ranwhat/backups`.
- `ranwhat sources`: every coding agent ranwhat reads, where it looked for each one's history, and whether it found any. `check`, `watch` and `clean` read them all by default; `--source ID` reads one, and `--path ID=PATH` reads one from elsewhere.
- `ranwhat scan profile.json`: scores authority, observability and reversibility for the credentials an agent holds. `--html report.html` writes a report. `--pull-usage` checks which grants were used, against the provider's own audit trail.
- `ranwhat live`: the same, from read-only token introspection. Pass tokens in the environment (`RANWHAT_GITHUB_TOKEN`, `RANWHAT_GOOGLE_TOKEN`, `RANWHAT_SLACK_TOKEN`, `RANWHAT_STRIPE_TOKEN`), not as flags.
- `ranwhat demo`: an authority scan on a bundled example, with no setup.
- `ranwhat hook install`: the one opt-in exception to after the fact. It adds a PreToolUse hook to Claude Code's settings (`--scope user`, `project` or `local`), and each tool call watch's rules rate high or critical then waits for the user's yes (`--mode ask`, the default) or, when critical, is refused (`--mode deny`). It judges locally and sends nothing; a call no rule rates high or critical gets no answer, and if the hook fails the call goes ahead. `ranwhat hook status` shows where it is installed and `ranwhat hook uninstall` removes it. It needs a lasting install (`uv tool install`, `pipx install` or `pip install`), not `uvx`.
- `ranwhat update`: refreshes the capability catalogue. Needs a Plus subscription, which is live: €12 a month per organisation. On a terminal, `scan`, `live` and `update --status` may add one dim line about the feed on stderr, never with `--json`; `RANWHAT_NO_HINTS=1` turns it off.

Agents read: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, Cursor, Windsurf, Cline, Roo Code, OpenCode, Continue, Aider, Goose, Qwen Code, Grok Build, Droid, Kimi Code, Kimi CLI, Pi, Muse Code and OpenClaw. `check`, `watch` and `clean` read all twenty, each from where it keeps its history, for the last 30 days by default (`--days N`). For Claude Code that is `~/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl` and each session's `subagents/` transcripts, or the same under `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects` when that is set; `--root PATH` reads another directory. Databases and compressed files are only read: Cursor's and OpenClaw's histories are databases, so `clean` finds their secrets but cannot mask them there. Windsurf keeps Cascade's own history encrypted, so ranwhat reads the plaintext transcripts its `post_cascade_response_with_transcript` hook writes to `~/.windsurf/transcripts`. Meta Muse, Grok Bot and the current Amp keep their history in their vendor's cloud, so there is nothing local to read.

`check` and `watch` hide every secret `clean` finds, anywhere in the history whatever `--days` says, in what they print. They keep an index for that in `~/.ranwhat/known/` (`$RANWHAT_HOME/known/` when set): salted fingerprints, never a secret, readable by you alone.

Not read yet: large tool outputs Claude Code stores in `<session>/tool-results/`, `~/.claude/history.jsonl`, and the events OpenClaw stores compressed and its cold transcript archives. Compressed Codex sessions (`.jsonl.zst`) are read on Python 3.14, or with the `zstd` command on the PATH.

## Docs

- [Commands](https://ranwhat.com/commands): every command and every flag, what each reads and what it sends
- [watch](https://ranwhat.com/watch): the nine rules, their severities, the false positives it suppresses, and where it reads from
- [clean](https://ranwhat.com/clean): how secrets are found, why masking is not remediation, and the review session
- [scan](https://ranwhat.com/scan): the three scores, evidence states, and the providers the catalogue covers
- [Install](https://ranwhat.com/install): uvx, pipx or pip, and what it reads and writes
- [FAQ](https://ranwhat.com/faq): what it reads, what it sends, what masking does, and where it fits in AI agent security, secret scanning and OPSEC
- [README](https://github.com/MatijaMiki/ranwhat/blob/main/README.md): full command reference in Markdown

## Guides

- [Guides](https://ranwhat.com/guides): every guide, with a one-line summary
- [AI coding agent security](https://ranwhat.com/guides/ai-coding-agent-security): a checklist for AI agent security on your own machine: what a coding agent can reach, the boundary around it, what it writes to disk, auditing what it ran, and scoping its tokens
- [Claude Code history](https://ranwhat.com/guides/claude-code-history): where transcripts live, retention, and how to purge them, plus where Codex, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI and Qwen Code keep theirs
- [Stop Claude Code reading .env](https://ranwhat.com/guides/claude-code-env-secrets): Read deny rules, what they miss, the sandbox, and what to do once a secret was read
- [Claude Code audit log](https://ranwhat.com/guides/claude-code-audit-log): reading back what ran from the transcripts, then a hook or OpenTelemetry for a record from now on
- [Claude Code deleted my files](https://ranwhat.com/guides/claude-code-deleted-files): finding what was deleted and when, what rewind cannot restore, recovering from git or backups, and blocking a repeat
- [AI agent token scopes](https://ranwhat.com/guides/ai-agent-token-scopes): least privilege for an agent's tokens: checking what GitHub, Google, Slack, Stripe and AWS credentials allow and have used, then cutting them
- [Developer OPSEC](https://ranwhat.com/guides/developer-opsec): operations security for developers who use AI coding agents: where credentials sit on a laptop, what agent transcripts add, finding and rotating what is already there, and keeping secrets out of plaintext
